merger_description:
AbbVie Inc. (AbbVie) proposes to acquire all of the outstanding shares of Apogee Therapeutics, Inc. (Apogee) (the Acquisition).

AbbVie is a North Chicago-based, New York Stock Exchange-listed global biopharmaceutical company active in the development and supply of medicines and therapies across a range of therapeutic areas, including immunology, oncology, neuroscience, aesthetics and eye care. In Australia, AbbVie supplies Rinvoq, a Janus Kinase (JAK) inhibitor used to treat atopic dermatitis.

Apogee is a San Francisco-based, NASDAQ-listed clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing a pipeline of biologic therapies for inflammatory and immunological diseases, including atopic dermatitis, asthma, eosinophilic oesophagitis and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Apogee’s lead asset, zumilokibart (APG777), is a clinical-stage (Phase 2b) monoclonal antibody therapy that targets interleukin-13 (IL-13) for the treatment of atopic dermatitis. Apogee does not have any marketed products anywhere in the world.

AbbVie and Apogee overlap in the development of therapies for the treatment of atopic dermatitis.

determination_table_content.details:
AbbVie, Inc, via its wholly owned subsidiary Andor LLC (together,
AbbVie), proposes to acquire 100% of the outstanding shares in
Apogee Therapeutics, Inc. (Apogee) (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, AbbVie, is a North Chicago-based, New York Stock
Exchange-listed global biopharmaceutical company active in the
development and supply of medicines and therapies across a range
of therapeutic areas, including immunology, oncology, neuroscience,
aesthetics and eye care.
In Australia, AbbVie supplies Rinvoq, a Janus Kinase inhibitor used
to treat atopic dermatitis.
The target, Apogee, is a San Francisco-based, NASDAQ-listed
clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing a
pipeline of biologic therapies for inflammatory and immunological
diseases, including atopic dermatitis, asthma, eosinophilic
oesophagitis and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
Apogee’s lead asset, zumilokibart (APG777), is a clinical-stage
(Phase 2b) monoclonal antibody therapy that targets interleukin-13
(IL-13) for the treatment of atopic dermatitis. Apogee does not have
any marketed products anywhere in the world.

determination_table_content.item:
Overlap and relationship
between the Parties
determination_table_content.details:
AbbVie and Apogee overlap in the research and development of
therapies for the treatment of atopic dermatitis.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and publicly available information, as relevant.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• Rinvoq and APG777 are unlikely to be close substitutes,
given their differentiated mechanisms of action, safety
profiles, onset of action and methods of administration.
• There are other competitors who already supply, or are
active in the development of, atopic dermatitis therapies that
will continue to compete with the merged entity.
• The potential competition between the Parties in relation to
other pipeline products for the treatment of atopic
dermatitis is uncertain, given the early stages of the Parties’
respective pipeline products.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.
